Semenivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Semenivka's Jewish community, first documented in the first half of the 19th century, numbered 1,377 by the late 19th century, and withstood a pogrom in October 1905. During WWII, the entire Jewish population was resettled onto Kovalivka Street, forming a short-lived ghetto; on November 30, all were taken to a birch grove outside the city and shot, though the exact death toll can no longer be established. According to the Committee on the Preservation of Jewish Heritage, this cemetery once held gravestones dating from 1930 to 1937, though a 2020 ESJF survey could not locate them.
